links.comparator_used: Stand-alone question with no reading-level or audience instruction (also compared with prompt A, which had no length or grade-level limits)
links.outcome: Readability (average grade reading level) versus accuracy and comprehensiveness of LLM answers to retinal disease patient questions
links.effect: Average grade reading level 13.45 (stand-alone), 11.5 (prompt A), 10.3 (prompt B) (p < 0.001). Median accuracy 5.0, 5.0, 4.0 and median comprehensiveness 5.0, 5.0, 4.0 for stand-alone, prompt A, prompt B; prompt B accuracy and comprehensiveness lower (p < 0.001).
links.tradeoff: Specifying length and grade reading level (prompt B) lowered accuracy and comprehensiveness compared with stand-alone and prompt A.
links.quote: Prompt engineering can significantly improve readability of LLM-generated responses, although at the cost of reducing accuracy and comprehensiveness.

links.comparator_used: Stand-alone question with no audience, tone or reading-level specification (also compared with prompt A, which had no length or grade-level limits)
links.outcome: Readability (average grade reading level) versus accuracy and comprehensiveness of responses when length and reading level were specified
links.effect: Average grade reading level 13.45 (stand-alone), 11.5 (prompt A), 10.3 (prompt B) (p < 0.001). Median accuracy and comprehensiveness 5.0, 5.0, 4.0 for stand-alone, prompt A, prompt B; prompt B lower (p < 0.001).
links.tradeoff: Prompt B, with specified length and grade-level limits, reduced accuracy and comprehensiveness.
links.quote: The use of prompt B was associated with a lower accuracy and comprehensiveness than responses to stand-alone question or prompt A questions (p < 0.001).
